#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/kind api-change

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This promotes `CronJob` resource to `batch/v1` based on https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/19 and complete description from https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-apps/19-Graduate-CronJob-to-Stable 

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #90473

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
/assign @deads2k @liggitt 

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
The CronJob API is promoted to batch/v1. The batch/v1beta1 API version is deprecated and will no longer be served in 1.25.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:
```docs
- [KEP]: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-apps/19-Graduate-CronJob-to-Stable 
```

When will the controller change to use v1? Was that intended to happen in this PR or one that builds on top of this? 

Since conformance tests must pass on a cluster with [all beta APIs turned off](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-architecture/1333-conformance-without-beta), it would have to be done before promoting the e2e to conformance.

review_comments: exercise both the v1 and v1beta1 variants?
Done.
nit: replace all these checks with a single `cmp.Diff`?
I don't see any value in doing this.
The value is that as we add more fields to the API, the code of the test doesn't grow. Also it would gracefully handle nil pointers.
I think in those cases I think it's better being explicit and catch all mismatches during tests, not gracefully handle nil which should not happen.

`Diff` gives you a report of all the differences. When I say gracefully handle nil, I mean that it will report in one field is nil and not the other, but it won't crash. The existing code would just crash.
Yup, I'm aware of that :smile:
Then why is this not desired? We tend to advocate for `cmp.Diff` in scheduler tests as the code becomes easier to maintain. Are we missing something?
revert empty line, as this comment applies to all subsequent functions and not just the next one.
you can remove the mention of `v2alpha1` in the comment now
Updated both in the latest push.

is there an issue or project tracking the 1.22 items?

* Switch storage to batch/v1
* Switch `kubectl prune` (and addon manager prune whitelist) to batch/v1
Adding those to https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/19
`pointer.BoolPtr`
Updated.
was there any discussion of adding conditions to cronjob status? cc @deads2k
Nope, since the state of a particular instance is reflected through a job.
why the change?
We're not doing conversions like we did before and this field is missing from cronjob read from the server. It has to be set explicitly like in all other create commands.
Perhaps a more authoritative link is https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/crontab.html

Is there any technical reason to keep this as a pointer? Since the default is false, I don't think there is a need for this to be a pointer. Since we are graduating to v1, we can take the chance to simplify this and just make it a boolean. @liggitt wdyt?

@apelisse what's the current state of server-side apply dealing of a field like this? If this was `bool`, defaulted to `false` and was `omitempty`, a false value (whether it was the default or explicit from the user) wouldn't get serialized.

Would that make server-side apply think there was a change if the user applied an explicit `false` and it differed from the serialized value (which would omit `false`)?
ping @apelisse
I'll have to write a test for that, that's an interesting use-case. I'm afraid it'll fall in the "implicit normalization kubernetes does to objects" that server-side apply doesn't really like.
But that implicit normalization doesn't change if the field is a pointer or not. In both cases, during defaulting, we add a value. Unless you are referring to something else?
If the boolean isn't a pointer, it'll constantly get omitted, which means that SSA will remove the ownership of that field (because it disappeared).
I don't think it's terrible, it would prevent a conflict from happening if it's applied to false and later someone wants to apply true. The other way around will be fine.
I need to test, it's possible that this will force an etcd rewrite on any apply ... :-/ I think I know how we could fix that.
Any conclusions?
Since there is doubt, I would just use the pointer if that's fine with performance (which I'm sure it is).
FYI @adtac
does the controller tolerate this being unset on a successful job? a skewed API server where the final update was done against a 1.20 API server will have this blank
Yes, we're not using this value anywhere in the controller yet. It's there for information for users, only for now.
should this be replaced with an apps/v1 test?
yeah, good catch, fixed.
I don't see any validation added for this field. should there be any?
I don't expect this require any validation.
